title: Food & Restaurants
subtitle: Order, eat, and pay like a local
description: Whether it's a Darshini, a mess, or a fancy restaurant — these phrases handle ordering, dietary preferences, and the bill.

items.context: Koḍi means please give — this polite suffix works with almost anything you want to ask for
items.scenario: Sitting down at any restaurant that isn't a self-service Darshini — the menu may only be a laminated paper sheet

items.context: Point at what you want and say this — works in restaurants, street stalls, and anywhere without a price board
items.scenario: Pointing at a dish you can see others eating but don't know the name of, or checking the price before ordering
items.imageQuery: price check pointing food stall india

items.context: Śāka means vegetable, āhāri means eater — vegetarianism is widely respected in Karnataka and most places accommodate it easily
items.scenario: Whenever you sit down somewhere new — say this once and the staff will guide you to the right dishes

items.context: Māṃsa means meat — some traditional restaurants only serve vegetarian food, so knowing this helps you understand if you're in the right place
items.scenario: Asking if a restaurant serves meat dishes, or clarifying your preference when being recommended a place

items.context: Kāra is spice/heat, kammi means less, māḍi means make — Karnataka food can be genuinely fiery, especially sambar and chutneys
items.scenario: When ordering at a Darshini or mess and you want to warn the cook that you're not built for full-heat Karnataka spice
items.imageQuery: spicy food chilli heat warning india

items.context: Nīru is water — one of the most essential words in the language and the most requested thing at any Karnataka meal
items.scenario: At any restaurant, mess, or even a roadside stall — always ask for water before the spicy food arrives

items.context: Innu means more/still, svalpa means a little — in traditional Karnataka meals, refills are free and expected. Don't be shy
items.scenario: At a banana leaf meal or mess where rice and sambar are refilled — point at what you want more of
items.imageQuery: food refill more serving banana leaf

items.context: Sāku means enough — say this with your hand out, palm facing down, when you want the server to stop refilling
items.scenario: When the server keeps piling rice onto your banana leaf and you're already full but they won't stop

items.context: Ruci means taste, tumba means very — saying this to a restaurant owner or home cook is one of the nicest things you can do
items.scenario: After a good meal anywhere — the cook's face will light up when a non-Kannadiga says this genuinely
items.imageQuery: delicious food happy eating thumbs up

items.context: Simple and understood everywhere — at sit-down restaurants you need to ask, servers won't bring it automatically
items.scenario: When you've finished eating and are ready to pay — don't wait, just ask

items.context: Ūṭa means a proper meal (cooked rice with sides) — asking this at a mess or hotel unlocks the full banana-leaf experience rather than just ordering à la carte
items.scenario: Walking into a local mess or 'hotel' (as restaurants are called in Karnataka) and asking if the full meal is available

items.context: Filter coffee in Karnataka is a ritual — thick decoction, hot milk, served in a steel davara-tumbler set. Nothing else compares
items.scenario: At any 'hotel' or Darshini in Karnataka — this is the correct move every morning
items.imageQuery: filter coffee south india steel tumbler

items.context: Ideyā turns a statement into a question — use it to ask if any dish is available before ordering it
items.scenario: At a small street stall or mess that might only serve specific items depending on the time of day
items.imageQuery: idli dosa south indian breakfast plate

items.context: Parcel is the Karnataka word for takeaway — māḍi means do/make it. Perfectly understood everywhere from Darshinis to highway dhabas
items.scenario: When you want to take food back to your hostel or PG instead of eating in
items.imageQuery: takeaway pack food parcel bag india

items.context: Chenna means beautiful or excellent in Kannada — a warm all-purpose compliment that works for food, places, and people
items.scenario: After finishing a meal at a small local restaurant — the chef and owner will remember you fondly
items.imageQuery: excellent nice happy satisfied food compliment
